title: A Cloud That Followed a Boy

before.title: A Cloud That Followed a Boy
before.text:
Ever since he was young, a small gray cloud followed Diego wherever he went. It rained only above him, never on anyone else nearby.

His friends teased him gently, calling him "the boy with his own weather." Diego felt embarrassed, wishing the cloud would simply disappear.

One rainy afternoon, a little girl fell into a pond near the village. Nobody else was close enough to help quickly.

Diego ran over, and his cloud suddenly poured heavy rain, raising the pond's water level just enough for the girl to reach the edge safely.

After that day, Diego stopped feeling embarrassed. His strange little cloud had finally proven useful, and he thanked it quietly every single day.

after.text:

One hot afternoon, he passed the school garden. The soil was dry, and the young plants were drooping. Diego stood among the young plants. His cloud rained over him and the soil at his feet. He walked carefully between the rows, watering each one.

The next day, the plants stood taller. Diego told his friends what had happened. When the garden became dry again, he returned with his cloud. He no longer wished it away.

title: A Trip to Grandma's

before.title: A Trip to Grandma's
before.text:
Every summer, Leo visited his grandmother in the countryside. He always looked forward to the long car ride. He played games and ate snacks along the way.

Grandma's house smelled like fresh bread. Her garden was full of bright flowers and buzzing bees.

This year, Grandma taught Leo how to bake simple cookies. She explained each step, and Leo mixed the ingredients himself.

They spent the afternoon together in the kitchen. They laughed whenever flour landed on their clothes.

At the end of the visit, Leo took home a small bag of cookies. He also carried a happy memory that would last until his next visit.

before.text: The yard behind Emma's new home was full of tall grass and weeds. She wanted a garden, but the work looked too large. An older neighbor came over with gloves and two tools. title: Wishing Bench

before.title: Wishing Bench
before.text: An old bench stood beside the town bakery. People said that a wish made there would come true, but only if it helped someone else. Josef wished for more customers at his small shop. The next day, a parade closed the main road and brought many people past his door. He sold everything. Then he remembered the rule. Josef used part of the money to repair the broken bench. After that, people sat there to rest, talk, and share food. His wish lasted because he made room for other people's wishes too.

title: Community Garden Plot

before.text: Nora received a small plot in the community garden. She planted tomatoes, but the young plants soon bent toward a fence. The next plot had more sun. Its gardener explained that tomatoes needed several hours of direct light. He helped Nora move two plants and showed her how to water near the roots. In return, Nora cared for his plot while he was away. By summer, both gardens were full of fruit. The shared advice was as useful as the shared land.

title: The House That Moved at Night

before.title: The House That Moved at Night
before.text:
Every evening, Hana walked past the same empty house on her way home.

One morning, she noticed something strange. The house was on the other side of the road.

At first, Hana thought she was confused. But the next day, the house stood beside the river.

That night, she decided to watch.

Just after midnight, the windows began to glow. The house lifted slowly from the ground on four wooden legs.

It walked across the field without making a sound.

Hana followed from a distance.

The house stopped near an old woman carrying a heavy bag. Its front door opened. The woman went inside.

By morning, the house had moved near the town hospital.

Hana finally understood. The house was not lost.

It moved to places where someone needed a warm room for the night.

After that, Hana stopped asking where the house belonged.

She only wondered who would need it next.

title: The Boy Who Borrowed a Cloud

before.title: The Boy Who Borrowed a Cloud
before.text:
A dry summer lasted for many weeks.

Kai watched the fields turn brown. His family needed rain, but every day the sky stayed clear.

One evening, Kai climbed a hill and found a small cloud caught between two trees.

The cloud was no bigger than a car.

Kai pulled it free with a long branch.

“Can you come with me?” he asked.

The cloud followed him down the hill.

When they reached the fields, Kai asked it to rain.

A few drops fell. Then the cloud became smaller.

Kai realized that the cloud did not have enough water for the whole valley.

So he led it to the sea.

There the cloud grew larger as warm air rose from the water.

The next day, it returned with many other clouds.

Rain fell across the valley for hours.

Kai never said that he had made the rain.

He only smiled when people looked at the dark sky with relief.

title: A Phone Call from an Old Friend

before.title: A Phone Call from an Old Friend
before.text:
Mika was washing dishes when her phone rang.

The name on the screen surprised her.

It was Rina, a friend from school whom she had not spoken to for five years.

At first, both of them sounded a little nervous.

They asked the usual questions about work, family, and where they lived.

Then Rina mentioned a teacher they both remembered.

Mika laughed.

Soon they were talking about small things from the past: a rainy school trip, a terrible lunch, and a song they used to hear every morning.

Forty minutes passed.

Nothing important had happened during the call.

Neither friend asked for help or made a big announcement.

Still, after they said goodbye, Mika felt lighter.

She realized that some friendships do not disappear completely when people stop meeting.

Sometimes they only become quiet.

One unexpected call can make the old connection visible again.

title: The Umbrella Left at the Cafe

before.title: The Umbrella Left at the Cafe
before.text:
Taro noticed the umbrella only after the cafe had closed.

It was dark green and still hanging beside his table.

He almost took it home.

It was raining, and he had forgotten his own umbrella.

But the name “M. Sato” was written inside the handle.

Taro left the umbrella with a note for the morning staff and ran to the station in the rain.

The next afternoon, he returned to the cafe.

A woman at the next table stood up.

“Are you the person who found my umbrella?” she asked.

She had come back looking for it.

Taro said he had only left it where she could find it.

The woman bought him a coffee anyway.

They talked for ten minutes before leaving.

Taro had arrived wet the night before because he did not take someone else’s umbrella.

The small inconvenience had turned into a pleasant meeting.

title: The Clock That Paused

before.title: The Clock That Paused
before.text:
At exactly four each afternoon, the clock above Bell Street stopped for seven minutes. Buses arrived late, cakes burned in ovens, and people blamed their watches.

Only Rosa noticed that the whole street became still. Pigeons hung in the air. Rain stopped between the clouds and the ground. Rosa could move, but no one else could.

During those seven minutes, she began doing small jobs. She moved a ball away from a car, closed a window before rain entered, and returned a dropped letter to a mail bag.

One afternoon, the clock did not stop. Life continued at its usual speed. Rosa missed the silence, but then she saw a boy's ball roll toward the road. This time, she did not need magic. She called out, and he caught it.

title: The Bridge of Feathers

before.title: The Bridge of Feathers
before.text:
The valley had no bridge, and the river was too wide to cross. Each autumn, silver birds rested there before flying south.

Mara watched them leave feathers on the shore. She gathered the feathers and tied them together with grass. Her first bridge blew away. The second fell into the water.

For the third, the people in the village helped. Kids sorted feathers, fishers made strong ropes, and builders fixed the ends to stone. By sunset, a pale bridge floated above the river.

It held because every feather shared the weight. The silver birds returned in spring and circled over it. From high above, the bridge looked like one of their wings.

title: A Map Made of Song

before.title: A Map Made of Song
before.text:
Ivo inherited a map with no lines or names. When he sang beside it, a blue path appeared across the paper.

He followed the path into the hills. Whenever it divided, he sang again. A low note showed the road to the river; a high note pointed toward a village. After three days, his voice grew tired, and the map remained blank.

An old shepherd invited him to rest. She knew the path through the mountains and walked with him the next morning. Ivo learned the sound of water under stones and the shape of clouds before snow.

When he at last reached the sea, the map was still almost empty. He understood that it had never meant to replace local knowledge. It had only helped him begin asking for it.

title: The Baker of Dreams

before.title: The Baker of Dreams
before.text:
Each night, Leni baked dreams in the oven behind her shop. Round dreams brought peaceful sleep. Long, thin dreams carried people to distant places.

One evening, the mayor ordered a dream of victory. Leni mixed bright sugar and strong spice, but the dough would not rise. She tried again, with the same result.

A tired street cleaner entered and asked for any dream left over. Leni gave him a plain piece made with warm milk. He slept beside the stove and dreamed that the whole town planted trees together.

In the morning, he told the mayor. The mayor forgot about victory and asked where they should begin digging. Leni kept the failed dough as a reminder: some dreams cannot be made to order.
